failures.title: Read cache served one file's bytes for another
failures.symptom: The injection harness, which invokes probes directly and writes every generated case to the same path, was served the previous case's text; recall on four rules read 0.0000 and the harness reported the number without complaint.
failures.how_detected: injection-harness recall figures (relayed from the offline bundle session; not reproduced on this machine)
failures.root_cause: `_READ_CACHE` in probes.py keyed on path alone and depended on every caller clearing it between scans; the harness never calls run_scan, so nothing cleared it.
failures.fix_summary: The cache key is now (path, st_mtime_ns, st_size) with a bounded size, so the cache cannot be wrong regardless of who calls it.
failures.prevention_notes: The test calls probes._read directly with no scan and no clearing call, exactly as the harness does. Fix landed in the offline bundle (8775017..54f9a13), which predates this shallow clone, so no SHA is cited.

failures.title: tools/*.sh shebang indented, scripts not runnable as scripts
failures.symptom: The four tools/*.sh scripts were not recognised by the kernel as scripts whatever their mode bit said: `#!/usr/bin/env bash` had been indented by two spaces.
failures.how_detected: reading the bundle diffs while recording ARB-007
failures.root_cause: An earlier commit indented the shebang line; a shebang is only honoured at byte 0 of the file.
failures.fix_summary: Restored the shebang at column 0 and the executable bits on the four scripts.
failures.no_test_reason: No test reads the scripts' first line or mode bits; the CHANGELOG records the repair from the bundle diff only.
failures.prevention_notes: Fix landed in the offline bundle, which predates this shallow clone; no SHA is cited.

failures.title: Adapter timeout crashed instead of killing the analyzer on Windows
failures.symptom: On Windows every adapter timeout raised AttributeError out of the cleanup path (`signal.SIGKILL` does not exist there) and the analyzer ran on past the timeout meant to stop it.
failures.how_detected: by hand on a Windows developer machine; no automation had ever run on Windows
failures.root_cause: `Adapter._kill_group` named `signal.SIGKILL` unconditionally and relied on `os.setsid`/`os.killpg`, none of which exist on Windows, so the process-group guarantee the timeout depends on had no implementation there. CI was ubuntu-only with no matrix.
failures.fix_summary: `_kill_group` delegates to a new `Adapter._kill_tree` when `os.killpg` is absent; it runs `taskkill /T /F /PID` and falls back to `proc.kill()` if taskkill is missing or fails. The one-line `getattr(_signal, 'SIGKILL', SIGTERM)` repair was rejected because signalling the direct child alone leaves fanned-out workers running. POSIX path unchanged.
failures.prevention_notes: The four no-process-group tests were added by ARB-024 (5f92818, 2026-09-14), which also made pr-check.yml a ubuntu/windows matrix with fail-fast false; they delete os.killpg so the fallback runs on Linux too. Residual risk: taskkill /T cannot reach a grandchild already orphaned by an exited intermediate process. The ARB-006 fix commit predates this shallow clone.

failures.title: Doc-reference drift rule reported every dotted path as missing
failures.symptom: `drift.doc-references-missing-file` produced 187 of 230 unsuppressed findings in a self-scan (81%), every dotted path in the repository reading as missing; all 20 findings already queued for adjudication were among them.
failures.how_detected: reading the evidence while preparing the first adjudication queue from a self-scan; measured by scanning Arbiter with itself before and after
failures.root_cause: The rule normalised a backtick-quoted path with `lstrip("./")`, which strips a character set rather than a prefix, so `.ai/context-brief.md` became `ai/context-brief.md` and neither the exact nor the suffix membership test could match.
failures.fix_summary: The rule uses `_normalize_relative()`, the helper the sibling link rule in probes.py already used, and skips paths that escape the repository root; 187 findings to 28.
failures.prevention_notes: Adjudicating the queue first would have spent a fifth of the rule's lifetime evidence (MIN_OBSERVATIONS 20) recording a bug permanently, since record() refuses re-adjudication. Lesson recorded in project-context: measure a rule by running the scanner, not an out-of-band script. Fix commit predates this shallow clone.

failures.title: Arbiter's own artifacts written in the console codepage on Windows
failures.symptom: A generated review-queue.md was undecodable as UTF-8 on Windows: byte 0x97, an em dash written as cp1252.
failures.how_detected: reading the first calibration queue back on a Windows machine
failures.root_cause: Thirteen `write_text()` calls across cli.py, report.py, engine.py and learn.py omitted `encoding=`, so the HTML, markdown, PR-comment and review-queue renderings took the platform default. JSON writers escaped non-ASCII and were unaffected but were made explicit too.
failures.fix_summary: Every write of an Arbiter-authored artifact, and the matching reads, name encoding='utf-8'.
failures.prevention_notes: ARB-009 deliberately left the target-file readers and the YAML/TOML config readers alone; both came back (FAIL-007, FAIL-033). The invariants test, added by ARB-030, walks src/ with ast rather than covering the known sites. Fix commit predates this shallow clone.

failures.title: A scan read its own output directory
failures.symptom: Two identical self-scans differed: the second reported on the first's rendering. 28 of 101 unsuppressed findings (27.7%) sat inside arbiter-out, 24 of them `assurance.blanket-suppression`, the rule about to be adjudicated, because a report is full of the strings that rule searches for.
failures.how_detected: before/after figures for ARB-008 refused to reconcile
failures.root_cause: `--out` defaults to `arbiter-out`, a relative path inside the tree being scanned, and the walk knew nothing about it, so the previous run's report.json and review-queue.md were read as source.
failures.fix_summary: `run_scan` takes `out_dir`, threads it through inventory building, and `walk_repo` skips the resolved output directory. Two consecutive scans into the default path now produce identical findings.
failures.prevention_notes: Only the current run's out_dir is excluded here; a leftover directory under another --out name came back as FAIL-028 (ARB-029). Fix commit predates this shallow clone.

failures.title: Scanned files decoded under the platform default codec
failures.symptom: An em dash in a scanned file reached a generated review queue as `â€”`.
failures.how_detected: reading the first adjudication queue closely
failures.root_cause: Nine target-file read sites used `read_text(errors="replace")` with no encoding, so the codec was the platform default (cp1252 on Windows), which decodes nearly every byte without raising. ARB-009 had excluded these sites on the stated reasoning that errors='replace' was the design intent; the intent was never crashing on a target file, which encoding='utf-8' preserves.
failures.fix_summary: All target-file reads pass encoding='utf-8' with errors='replace' retained.
failures.prevention_notes: Project-context records that the mistake was a stated justification that had not been checked, not an oversight. The records name graph.py and review_ui.py as the target-file readers; the other sites are not named individually. Fix commit predates this shallow clone.

failures.title: Documented files under SKIP_DIRS reported as missing
failures.symptom: Documentation naming tracked files under .arbiter/ (knowledge.json, external-severity.json) was reported as drift: 8 of 31 doc-drift findings on a self-scan, all false.
failures.how_detected: reading the 28 findings that survived the ARB-008 fix; omni doctor independently confirmed the 22 genuine ones
failures.root_cause: The doc-reference rule resolved paths against ctx.inventory.files, and directories in inventory.SKIP_DIRS never enter the inventory, so 'absent' and 'deliberately not walked' were indistinguishable. The sibling broken-link rule had the identical defect fifteen lines away.
failures.fix_summary: Both rules in probe_doc_drift confirm existence on disk before reporting. .arbiter/baseline.json, documented but genuinely absent, still reports, which is the evidence the fix is precise rather than blanket.
failures.prevention_notes: Fix commit predates this shallow clone.

failures.title: Doc-drift findings rendered without a repository
failures.symptom: All 330 doc-drift findings in a 36-repository corpus scan rendered as bare paths in the review queue; two repositories each contain a python/ tree, so a line naming a README under it identified no repository a reader could open.
failures.how_detected: the first corpus-scale review queues
failures.root_cause: `Location.short()` builds its repo:path prefix from the Location, and the three doc_drift construction sites set repo_id on the Finding only. The requirement as first written claimed the sibling probes already did this correctly; measurement showed the reverse (secrets 0 of 377 attributed, supply_chain 0 of 1,817, resource_policy 7 of 1,040).
failures.fix_summary: The three doc_drift Finding sites in probes.py pass repo_id into the Location.
failures.prevention_notes: First of three fixes for the same missing repo_id (FAIL-010, FAIL-011); ARB-030 later made attribution a standing invariant over whole-scan output. Fix commit predates this shallow clone.

failures.title: Review queue could not name the repository for most probes
failures.symptom: 3,227 of 3,564 findings in the corpus scan carried a blank Location.repo_id (supply_chain 0 of 1,817, secrets 0 of 377, resource_policy 7 of 1,040), so review-queue lines named no repository.
failures.how_detected: measuring every probe after FAIL-009 showed doc_drift was not the outlier
failures.root_cause: Roughly twenty Location construction sites across eight probes omitted repo_id; only assurance set it everywhere. The Finding carried the id in all 3,564 cases.
failures.fix_summary: `review.where()` qualifies the path from the Finding's repo_id when the Location is blank, without double-prefixing one that carries it; both the markdown and HTML (review_ui) front ends use it. The probe sites were left wrong and recorded as residual risk, so SARIF, HTML and console output stayed unqualified.
failures.prevention_notes: Measured afterwards: 120 of 120 queue lines name their repository, checked against real corpus directory names after an earlier regex-based measurement proved wrong. Fix commit predates this shallow clone.

failures.title: Probe construction sites omitted repo_id; two guessed the wrong repository
failures.symptom: SARIF, the HTML report and console output stayed unqualified after FAIL-010. The interface permission-unused finding attributed itself to the alphabetically first infrastructure repository, and one repository's LICENSE satisfied a house_rules required-path rule for all thirty-six.
failures.how_detected: closing the residual risk ARB-015 recorded
failures.root_cause: Eighteen construction sites in probes.py had the id in scope on the enclosing Finding but never passed it to the Location. The interface rule collected IAM service names into a set and discarded the grant site; the two house_rules path rules matched against every path in the scan flattened into one set and set no repo_id at all.
failures.fix_summary: Every Location built in probes.py carries its Finding's repo_id; granted_services records a Location so the finding cites the file of the grant; file_exists/file_absent are evaluated per repository. Re-measured: 3,564 findings before and after, unattributed 3,227 to 0, no finding changed repository.
failures.prevention_notes: Behaviour change recorded as risk: file_absent/file_exists now report per repository. Core.Location.__post_init__ records that per-site fixes were missed at one site in ARB-014, every probe in ARB-015, the sites again in ARB-016 and the adapters in ARB-029, which is why ARB-030 moved normalisation to one boundary. Fix commit predates this shallow clone.

failures.title: Review sampler measured repositories rather than rules
failures.symptom: Of six review queues drawn from the 36-repository corpus, resource.k8s-no-security-context took 19 of 20 findings from one repository and all 20 from teaching material the corpus tooling calls useless as a false-positive measure; unencrypted-database 18 of 20 and private-key 16 of 20 from one repository each.
failures.how_detected: measuring the six queues drawn after FAIL-010
failures.root_cause: `review.select()` ordered findings within a rule so that distinct files came first, which one repository satisfies on its own; the ledger records a verdict against the rule, so twenty marks from one repository would have been laundered into a rule precision figure and then into the gate.
failures.fix_summary: select() round-robins across repositories and keeps file spread as the secondary axis inside each; population is deliberately not an input, since that label lives in tools/corpus.py and the library must not import the test harness. Average distinct repositories per queue 6.0 to 12.2, largest single-repository share 64.2% to 30.0%.
failures.prevention_notes: The six old queues were regenerated; they were 120 of 120 lines blank, so nothing human was lost. Spread cannot exceed the pool: unencrypted-database still draws 18 of 20 from terragoat because only three corpus repositories produce it. Fix commit predates this shallow clone.

failures.title: Hosted API endpoints broken by string annotations in api.py
failures.symptom: Every upload to /v1/scan and /v1/gate failed inside body validation, and /v1/review-queue read its body as a query parameter and rejected all JSON; all three real endpoints were broken.
failures.how_detected: the first tests to drive the assembled application through a real request (two of twelve new tests failed on arrival)
failures.root_cause: `from __future__ import annotations` makes every annotation in api.py a string, which FastAPI resolves against the module's globals; `UploadFile` and the `ReviewRequest` body model are local to `create_app` by design, so neither could be found. Nothing had ever exercised create_app.
failures.fix_summary: Both names are published to the module when the app is built. Thirteen tests now go through a real request; httpx2 was added to the dev extra so they run rather than skip.
failures.prevention_notes: The cited tests post a multipart upload and a JSON body through starlette's TestClient, which is the path that failed; none is named after this defect.

failures.title: A clean report asked for its review queue got a 400 naming a server path
failures.symptom: A caller with a report holding no findings left to review, the good outcome, received HTTP 400 whose message named a server temporary directory.
failures.how_detected: the same first real-request tests as FAIL-013
failures.root_cause: `arbiter review` exits 0 and writes no file when a report has no findings or every finding is already adjudicated; `service.review_queue` treated the missing file as a failure.
failures.fix_summary: service.review_queue returns an empty queue (entry_count 0, recorded false) when there is nothing to review, with no server path in the body.
failures.prevention_notes: The empty-queue case is now an explicit branch in service.review_queue with its own test; the general rule is that an absent output file is a result to interpret, not an error to forward, and no server path may appear in an HTTP response body.

failures.title: arbiter mcp stdio server broken against every mcp SDK 2.x
failures.symptom: `arbiter mcp` raised AttributeError at startup: `@server.list_tools()` no longer exists on the installed SDK 2.2.0.
failures.how_detected: building the HTTP transport under ARB-010; no test had ever started the server
failures.root_cause: The SDK moved handlers from decorators to constructor arguments at 2.0, inside the old `mcp>=1.0` pin's own range. `TOOLS` is plain data so the schema tests passed without the SDK, and nothing ever spoke to the server.
failures.fix_summary: Pin raised to mcp>=2.2; `_build_server` builds both transports one way; a refusing tool returns with is_error set; one test starts `arbiter mcp` as a subprocess and speaks MCP down the pipes (initialize, list tools, a success, a refusal).
failures.prevention_notes: The SDK moved again on 2026-09-16 (23bc43e): _build_server now introspects Server.__init__ at runtime, and ARB-025 made omni doctor build the server for real rather than grep .mcp.json.

failures.title: Nightly training job committed nothing: training/ was gitignored
failures.symptom: Run 1 measured for fifty-five minutes and committed nothing: `git add -A .arbiter training` exited 1 and the step's `bash -e` failed the job two seconds after the cycle finished. The failure read as though the measurement had broken rather than the bookkeeping.
failures.how_detected: the first nightly run's log
failures.root_cause: `.gitignore` listed `training/`, which ignores the directory itself, so the add matched an ignore entry and git exited 1.
failures.fix_summary: `training/*` is ignored with negations for WORKLIST.md, fix-pairs.json and disagreements.json, so the accumulating files are tracked while stamped per-run logs stay out.
failures.prevention_notes: Repaired on 2026-09-13 as unplanned work with no requirement covering the job; ARB-023 (9bd5e3b, 2026-09-14) was created to own it and added tools/check_writeback.sh, which runs before the cycle in CI and in train_cycle.sh, plus a rebase before push. No commit in this shallow clone touches .gitignore on 2026-09-13, so no SHA is cited.

failures.title: Nightly job overwrote the handoff it exists to produce
failures.symptom: Every night the complete training/WORKLIST.md that train_cycle.sh had just written was overwritten with one headed 'Incomplete: no results found for corpus, discrimination'.
failures.how_detected: reading the nightly job's output after FAIL-016
failures.root_cause: The workflow's final step read /tmp/corpus-out/summary.json and /tmp/discriminate.json, which nothing writes.
failures.fix_summary: The step reads the newest stamped files under training/ and still runs on failure, so a cycle that dies early leaves a handoff from what did finish.
failures.no_test_reason: The repair is a workflow step that only runs in CI; no test reads train.yml's final step or its path discovery.
failures.prevention_notes: Unplanned repair; ARB-023 later gave the job a contract. No commit in this shallow clone carries the change.

failures.title: Fix-pair mining found nothing because the corpus was cloned shallow
failures.symptom: Fix-pair mining reported '0 candidate fix pairs from 41 repositories in 0s' every night: every repository skipped.
failures.how_detected: reading the nightly job's output after FAIL-016
failures.root_cause: The corpus was cloned at depth 1 and `tools/fixpairs.py` skips a shallow clone. Those pairs are the only ground truth in the system Arbiter did not generate itself.
failures.fix_summary: fetch_corpus.sh clones 300 commits deep, deepens clones already on disk and records the depth reached; train_cycle.sh runs it every cycle rather than only when the corpus is missing.
failures.no_test_reason: Needs the cloned corpus and network access; the suite skips the corpus-dependent test when the corpus is not cloned.
failures.prevention_notes: Unplanned repair; ARB-023 later gave the job a contract. No commit in this shallow clone carries the change.

failures.title: Migrated knowledge ledger saved still declaring schema 1
failures.symptom: A schema 1 ledger read and re-saved was written back with schema_version 1: the migration happened and then denied itself.
failures.how_detected: the migration test ARB-020 required
failures.root_cause: `Knowledge.from_dict` carried the file's schema_version forward instead of returning a current-schema object.
failures.fix_summary: from_dict always returns a current-schema object (KNOWLEDGE_VERSION 2). Nothing outside learn.py reads the field, so the blast radius was future migrations.
failures.prevention_notes: schema_version feeds version_hash(), so the committed ledger moved k:0f258c4ce717 to k:a37f38560140 with no evidence change; pinned scans had to be re-pinned.

failures.title: Partial-scan skip reason made a false claim about external analyzers
failures.symptom: Every repo-scoped probe skipped in a partial scan printed 'this check reads relationships between files and cannot answer from a subset', which is true of the native probes and false of semgrep and the other external analyzers, held back only because subset-exactness is unmeasured.
failures.how_detected: declaring adapter scope under ARB-022
failures.root_cause: `Probe` carried one skip reason for every repo-scoped probe; adapter-backed probes inherited the native probes' explanation along with the scope default.
failures.fix_summary: `Probe.scope_reason` carries the real reason, defaulted to the relationships wording for native probes and overridden by `adapters.SCOPE_REASON` for adapters; docs/ci.md and RUNNING-ON-YOUR-OWN-CODE.md now say a pull-request gate runs no third-party analyzer.
failures.prevention_notes: Nothing about what runs changed; the limit was made visible with an honest reason.

failures.title: A library's PEM-parsing source reported as a leaked private key
failures.symptom: ecdsa's own keys.py and packaging metadata, vendored in a CDK Lambda asset bundle, were reported as committed private keys: 3 critical findings on a real system scan.
failures.how_detected: running Arbiter as a system over two real repositories (STEP-Migration + STEP_App) rather than the fixture corpus
failures.root_cause: `_pem_has_key_material` judged a PEM block real if any text in the ~4000 characters after a BEGIN marker contained a colon, a check meant to allow encrypted-key preambles (Proc-Type: 4,ENCRYPTED) but satisfied by ordinary code and prose.
failures.fix_summary: It walks forward line by line and stops at the first line that is not base64 or a Key: value header, so surrounding text cannot manufacture a body.
failures.prevention_notes: One of three compounding gaps (FAIL-021..023); together the system scan went from 3 critical / 6,011 findings to 0 / 1,121.

failures.title: Renamed CDK output directory classified as first-party source
failures.symptom: A project using CDK_OUTDIR to redirect synth output to cdk.out.chk had everything inside it, including a Lambda asset bundle's vendored dependencies, classified role=source and scanned.
failures.how_detected: the same real-system scan as FAIL-021
failures.root_cause: `inventory.classify()` hardcoded the literal name cdk.out, and a branch-ordering bug meant even the unrenamed case would have classified the stack's own synthesized *.template.json as generated rather than the iac role that exempts nothing, losing ground truth SKIP_DIRS deliberately keeps.
failures.fix_summary: IAC_HINTS is checked first and both hint patterns accept a cdk.out* suffix.

failures.title: bandit and checkov walked vendored trees SKIP_DIRS excludes
failures.symptom: bandit produced 129,379 raw findings and consumed 669s of its 900s budget on one tree; a real system scan reported 6,011 findings, most from a vendored .venv and a Lambda asset bundle's dependencies.
failures.how_detected: the same real-system scan as FAIL-021
failures.root_cause: bandit and checkov each walk {workdir} with their own traversal, independent of inventory.SKIP_DIRS and of file roles.
failures.fix_summary: Both manifests invoke the tool with exclusions mirroring SKIP_DIRS, plus a cdk.out* pattern for bandit (it only reads Python) and a narrower asset.<hash> bundle pattern for checkov (which still needs the templates). bandit's runtime dropped from 669s to 4s.
failures.no_test_reason: The exclusions are argv in the adapter manifests and were verified empirically against a real vendored tree (the requirement's own acceptance criterion); exercising them needs bandit and checkov installed, which the suite does not assume.
failures.prevention_notes: Risk recorded on ARB-026: the lists mirror SKIP_DIRS by hand and can drift. semgrep was left uncovered and became FAIL-027 under ARB-029.

failures.title: MCP tests read pydantic alias names instead of attributes
failures.symptom: test_the_tool_schemas_still_build_against_the_installed_sdk and test_the_stdio_server_actually_starts_and_answers_a_real_client failed on main.
failures.how_detected: running the full suite during ARB-026; reproduced against plain main with ARB-026's changes stashed
failures.root_cause: The tests read .inputSchema, .serverInfo and .isError off objects the installed mcp SDK returns; those models take the camelCase alias on construction but expose the field as the snake_case Python attribute via an alias generator, confirmed from model_fields on the installed SDK.
failures.fix_summary: The two tests read .input_schema, .server_info and .is_error.
failures.prevention_notes: Test-only change. Commit 23bc43e the same day describes the SDK as having gone back to camelCase after a snake_case detour, which the ARB-027 record contradicts; the ledger follows the requirement entry and CHANGELOG.

failures.title: gitleaks wrote its report into the repository being scanned
failures.symptom: A file literally named `-`, full of gitleaks' own JSON output and so full of strings shaped like the secrets it finds, was created inside the scanned repository for the next scan of any repo to read as content.
failures.how_detected: continuing ARB-026's cross-repo scanning work outside the fixture corpus
failures.root_cause: gitleaks has no write-JSON-to-stdout mode; `--report-path -` was taken literally, and the adapter never set cwd so {workdir} was the default.
failures.fix_summary: `Adapter.invoke()` substitutes a private temp path for a {report_file} placeholder, reads it back once the process exits, and deletes it in a finally block.

failures.title: Backslash paths from checkov and bandit matched no suppress rule on Windows
failures.symptom: On Windows, path-based suppress rules silently matched zero checkov or bandit findings.
failures.how_detected: the same cross-repo scanning work as FAIL-025, on Windows
failures.root_cause: checkov and bandit hand back backslash-separated relative paths on Windows (checkov's even start with a bare leading backslash), while every suppress-rule glob and Location.path in the codebase assumes '/'.
failures.fix_summary: Adapter output paths are normalised to forward slashes before the existing './' stripping and before suppress-rule matching.
failures.prevention_notes: The cited test was added by ARB-030 and asserts the property over every finding of the fixture scans plus the Location boundary; ARB-029 shipped no test specific to adapter output. ARB-030 then moved separator normalisation into Location.__post_init__ (FAIL-029) so adapters and probes share one boundary.

failures.title: semgrep still walked vendored and CDK asset trees
failures.symptom: semgrep continued to scan vendored .venv and CDK asset-bundle trees after ARB-026 excluded them for bandit and checkov.
failures.how_detected: ARB-026's own risk notes, confirmed while continuing its cross-repo work
failures.root_cause: semgrep walks {workdir} with the same independent traversal as bandit and checkov; ARB-026 covered only those two.
failures.fix_summary: semgrep.adapter.toml carries the same exclusion list plus a cdk.out* pattern, since none of its configured rulesets understand CloudFormation templates either.
failures.no_test_reason: Manifest argv change, like FAIL-023; exercising it needs semgrep installed, which the suite does not assume.
failures.prevention_notes: Risk recorded on ARB-029: three separate fixed lists now mirror SKIP_DIRS and can drift independently.

failures.title: Leftover output directories under another --out name were scanned
failures.symptom: A fresh arbiter-out/ (or any untracked, .gitignore-matched directory) left over from a previous run under whatever --out name was given that time was read as source.
failures.how_detected: the same cross-repo scanning work as FAIL-025
failures.root_cause: SKIP_DIRS is a fixed name list and the ARB-011 exclusion covers only the current run's out_dir.
failures.fix_summary: `walk_repo` also excludes whatever `git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard --directory` reports, the plumbing incremental.py already uses for changed-file detection.
failures.no_test_reason: No test creates an ignored directory and asserts walk_repo skips it; tests/test_graph_system.py::test_output_directory_is_not_scanned covers only the current run's out_dir.

failures.title: Finding fingerprints differed between platforms
failures.symptom: The same finding had two identities, one per path-separator spelling: a verdict recorded on one platform could never match the same finding on another, and a baseline built on one reported every finding as new on the other. Nothing reported it.
failures.how_detected: the ARB-030 audit of the whole bug history
failures.root_cause: `Finding.fingerprint()` hashed location.path as written, so backslash and forward-slash spellings of one path hashed differently; adjudications are permanent and keyed by that fingerprint and record() refuses to re-adjudicate.
failures.fix_summary: Separator normalisation in `Location.__post_init__`, the boundary all ~54 construction sites pass through, rather than at each site, which is the form that was tried and missed in ARB-014, ARB-015, ARB-016 and ARB-029.
failures.prevention_notes: tools/mutate_tests.py ('path-separator') puts the defect back and requires the invariants test to fail; it runs in the pull-request check.

failures.title: Nightly external-severity measurement never reached the scanner
failures.symptom: Every nightly run since the tool was written measured 818 external checks and changed nothing; the 178 severities in the live ledger came from a one-off step that no longer exists.
failures.how_detected: the ARB-030 audit of every measurement tool
failures.root_cause: `tools/calibrate_external.py` wrote its measured severities to `.arbiter/external-severity.json` while `learn.apply()` read a flat map inside knowledge.json, and no code path moved a value from one to the other.
failures.fix_summary: `Knowledge.merge_external_severity()` merges the report into the ledger, storing no check the tool declined to grade; train_cycle.sh calls it after calibration. Merging the current report yields 288 entries, 110 of them checks that had no measured severity at all.
failures.prevention_notes: tools/mutate_tests.py ('ungraded-check-stored') covers the merge's refusal to store ungraded checks.

failures.title: calibrate_external.py documented a severity band its code cannot produce
failures.symptom: The module documented a >=50x -> high band that its own BANDS constant cannot produce and that its own prose says measurement is forbidden to claim.
failures.how_detected: the ARB-030 audit of every measurement tool
failures.root_cause: The documentation and the BANDS constant disagreed; the records do not say which changed first.
failures.fix_summary: The documentation now matches BANDS = [(10.0, 'medium'), (3.0, 'low')] with floor info, and states why measurement may not promote a check to high.
failures.prevention_notes: The cited test pins the code's ceiling at medium, which is what the stale documentation contradicted; the documentation text itself is not under test.

failures.title: UTF-16 files classified as binary and never read
failures.symptom: A credential in a file an editor saved as 'Unicode' (UTF-16 with a byte-order mark) was invisible: the file was classified as data and never read, a confident pass on a file that was never opened.
failures.how_detected: the new metamorphic encoding test written under ARB-030 found it immediately
failures.root_cause: `inventory._is_binary` treated any NUL byte as binary, and UTF-16 puts one between every ASCII character.
failures.fix_summary: A declared byte-order mark (_TEXT_BOMS) means text, and probes._decode honours the BOM when decoding. Headerless UTF-16 is still left as data on purpose: telling it from a real binary means guessing, and guessing wrong turns a binary into mojibake to scan.
failures.prevention_notes: tools/mutate_tests.py ('utf16-is-binary') puts the defect back and requires the metamorphic test to fail.

failures.title: Seven configuration reads used the platform default codec
failures.symptom: YAML and TOML configuration in policy.py, ab.py, controls.py, probes.py and adapters.py was read under the platform default codec, cp1252 on Windows, which mis-decodes silently rather than raising.
failures.how_detected: the new ast-walking encoding test written under ARB-030 found it immediately
failures.root_cause: The same defect as ARB-009 and ARB-012 in seven call sites those fixes did not touch; ARB-009 had explicitly left the config readers alone, noting adapters.py's TOML read as a latent defect of the same family.
failures.fix_summary: Each read names encoding='utf-8'; the new test walks src/ with ast and fails on any text read or write without an explicit encoding, rather than covering the sites that were known.
failures.prevention_notes: tools/mutate_tests.py ('implicit-encoding') removes one encoding= and requires the invariants test to fail.

failures.title: CRLF line endings dropped when file reading moved to bytes
failures.symptom: Six secret formats stopped being detected on any CRLF file: the rule that reads `name = value` ends at end of line and was seeing a trailing carriage return.
failures.how_detected: the existing suite caught it during ARB-030 before merge; the first regression test written for it used an AWS key, recognised by its own shape anywhere, and tools/mutate_tests.py reported that test as passing with the defect present
failures.root_cause: Moving file reading from read_text to bytes, which made the byte-order-mark check possible, silently dropped Python's newline translation with it.
failures.fix_summary: probes._decode normalises CRLF and lone CR to LF after decoding.
failures.prevention_notes: Introduced and fixed within ARB-030; it never reached main. tools/mutate_tests.py ('crlf-not-normalized') exists because the first test for this defect did not fail with the defect present: a test that has never failed is not evidence.

failures.title: Tests spawning bare 'bash' ran the WSL launcher on the Windows runner
failures.symptom: pr-check (windows-latest), first run: test_install_script_never_fails_a_build, test_bootstrap_refuses_when_it_is_not_a_repository and test_bootstrap_is_idempotent_about_an_existing_remote failed with exit 1 and a UTF-16 stdout reading 'Windows Subsystem for Linux has no installed distributions'.
failures.how_detected: CI, the first pull request to run the Windows matrix added in ARB-024
failures.root_cause: subprocess.run(['bash', ...]) hands the bare name to CreateProcess, which searches the System32 directory before PATH; System32\bash.exe is the WSL launcher, so Git Bash (on PATH) was never reached. shutil.which searches PATH only, which is why the writeback test that resolved bash that way passed on the same runner.
failures.fix_summary: A _bash() helper resolves the shell with shutil.which and skips only when none exists; the three tests use it.
failures.prevention_notes: Never spawn a shell or tool by bare name from a test or from src/: resolve it with shutil.which first. The same CreateProcess ordering bit ARB-006's taskkill path.

failures.title: The authored probe reported its own docstring's pattern list as three disabled TLS checks
failures.symptom: First self-gate: three high findings arbiter/authored.security-check-disabled at src/arbiter/authored.py:33-34, evidence verify=False, rejectUnauthorized: false, InsecureSkipVerify: true. Those lines are the module docstring listing what the probe looks for.
failures.how_detected: running arbiter gate on this repository for the first time (ARB-032)
failures.root_cause: _blank_comments blanks # comments for hash languages but not Python triple-quoted strings, so docstring prose was scanned as code. _strip_prose already blanked docstrings for the import scanner; the disabled-check scanner never got the same treatment.
failures.fix_summary: _blank_comments blanks triple-quoted strings for Python using the existing _PY_DOCSTRING regex.
failures.prevention_notes: Arbiter now gates its own pull requests (pr-check self-gate), so a probe that misreads its own source fails CI the day it ships.

failures.title: The no-bare-except house rule matched every except clause
failures.symptom: Self-scan: 89 house/no-bare-except findings under src/, including except OSError: and except BaseException: ... raise, none of them bare or broad.
failures.how_detected: self-scan triage (ARB-033)
failures.root_cause: The tree-sitter query was (except_clause) @hit with no predicate on the caught type, so it captured every handler; the title promised bare or broad.
failures.fix_summary: Query narrowed with (#match? @t ...) to Exception and BaseException; bare except: is left to ruff E722, which the pull-request job now installs.
failures.prevention_notes: A house rule earns its place by a test that plants the thing it names and one it does not; the rule shipped with neither.

failures.title: gitleaks findings on git-ignored and cache files reached the report as critical secrets
failures.symptom: First self-gate with the analyzers installed: 4 critical gitleaks findings, three of them on .ai/project-graph.json (git-ignored) and tests/__pycache__/*.pyc, files the inventory never scans.
failures.how_detected: running arbiter gate on this repository with tools/install_tools.sh applied (ARB-032)
failures.root_cause: Every adapter walks the tree itself. ARB-026 and ARB-029 taught bandit, checkov and semgrep the inventory's exclusions through their own flags; gitleaks was never taught, and adapter output was never checked against the inventory on the way in.
failures.fix_summary: Adapter.run keeps only findings whose path the inventory scanned (in_scope), so the boundary is enforced once for every tool rather than per manifest.
failures.prevention_notes: Scope is decided in one place, the inventory; a tool's own traversal is an implementation detail its output must be reconciled with.

failures.title: A missing python package read as not applicable, so the AST probes left the coverage denominator
failures.symptom: pr-check (windows-latest), no tree-sitter: test_a_dimension_with_no_basis_cannot_claim_complete failed because the coverage claim read 'not applicable here: ast_metrics, interface, house_rules_ast'. Two probes with a question to answer here were counted as having none.
failures.how_detected: CI, first Windows run after ARB-033 (the Linux job has tree-sitter)
failures.root_cause: Probe.applicable() answered two different questions with one False: a missing python module (prevented) and a single-repository or stack mismatch (nothing to assess). The engine set applicable=False for both, and the new coverage rule dropped both from the denominator. CI-12's reason check did not list 'missing python package'.
failures.fix_summary: Probe.prevented() reports missing modules and the engine records them as skipped with applicable=True, like a missing binary; applicable() keeps only the nothing-to-assess cases; CI-12 lists the new wording.
failures.prevention_notes: The Windows matrix is the machine without the optional dependency; a scoring rule that depends on applicability must be tested there, which the matrix now does on every pull request.

failures.title: The Python 3.10 CI cell segfaulted: checkov installs the pyston JIT into Arbiter's interpreter
failures.symptom: pr-check (ubuntu-latest, 3.10): pytest died with 'Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault' inside pytest's tmp_path fixture (posixpath.realpath), 'Extension modules: pyston, yaml._yaml', exit 139, after 25% of the suite.
failures.how_detected: pr-check on PR #5, the new 3.10 cell introduced by ARB-040
failures.root_cause: checkov==3.3.17 depends on pyston==2.3.5 and pyston-autoload on CPython < 3.11 (linux and macOS x86_64). tools/install_tools.sh installed checkov with plain pip into Arbiter's own interpreter, and pyston-autoload switches the JIT on in every process of that interpreter; pyston 2.3.5 crashes under pytest on 3.10. The 3.11 cells never saw it because the dependency marker excludes them.
failures.fix_summary: checkov is installed into its own venv (install_checkov_isolated, mirroring semgrep's isolation) with the launcher copied onto PATH, and any checkov, pyston and pyston-autoload left in Arbiter's interpreter are uninstalled.
failures.no_test_reason: The crash lives in a third-party JIT under a specific interpreter; the 3.10 CI cell is the regression test and runs on every pull request.
failures.prevention_notes: Every external analyzer that is a Python package is installed isolated from Arbiter's interpreter; a dependency marker that only fires on an older interpreter is why the matrix carries that interpreter.

failures.title: The cache digest was memoised on (path, mtime, size), so a same-size edit in one mtime tick was served stale
failures.symptom: pr-check (windows-latest, 3.11): tests/test_cache.py::test_an_edited_file_misses_the_cache failed: after rewriting b.py from 'y = 2' to 'y = 3' the cache key was unchanged.
failures.how_detected: pr-check on PR #5 (windows-latest), read by test name
failures.root_cause: file_digest memoised the sha256 under (abspath, st_mtime_ns, st_size). Windows reported the same mtime for two writes in quick succession, the size was identical, and the memo returned the previous digest, so the cache would have answered from the old findings.
failures.fix_summary: file_digest reads and hashes the bytes on every call; the memo table is gone. The cost is one read per file per cacheable probe, which the operating system cache absorbs.
failures.prevention_notes: A content key is computed from content; file metadata is never a proxy for it. The regression test pins the mtime so it fails on every platform if the memo returns.

failures.title: The stub detector matched a pass nested under except, so a real function was reported as a stub
failures.symptom: Code scanning on OmniEngineering PR #5 raised 'store_mcp_probe_memo is a stub' (arbiter/authored.stub-on-production-path) for a function that writes a JSON file and swallows a failed write with except OSError: pass.
failures.how_detected: code scanning alert from the SARIF the omni gate uploaded on OmniEngineering PR #5 (finding f:3780e4a24676)
failures.root_cause: _stubs searched the first eight body lines for any marker line (pass, ..., raise NotImplementedError, a temporary constant return) regardless of indentation, so a pass that was the body of a nested except, if or with branch counted as the body of the function.
failures.fix_summary: _stub_marker_at_body_level counts a marker only at the body's own indentation (the first statement after the docstring); a marker in a nested branch is ignored.
failures.prevention_notes: The regression test holds a function with a nested pass and asserts no stub finding, beside one whose whole body is pass and must still fire.

failures.title: The review-draft test compared a Windows path against a posix string
failures.symptom: pr-check (windows-latest, 3.11) on PR #6: tests/test_review_draft.py::test_the_knowledge_file_is_byte_identical_after_the_tool failed: {'out\\review-draft.md'} != {'out/review-draft.md'}.
failures.how_detected: pr-check on PR #6 (windows-latest), read by test name
failures.root_cause: The _tree helper built its set with str(path.relative_to(root)), which uses the platform separator; the expected value was written with a forward slash. The Linux run cannot see the difference.
failures.fix_summary: _tree returns relative_to(root).as_posix(), so the set compares the same on every platform.
failures.prevention_notes: A test that compares path strings builds them with as_posix() or compares Path objects; the Windows cell of pr-check is the control that catches the rest.

failures.title: use_adapters=False only skipped registration, so a scan that asked for no analyzers ran all five once another scan had registered them
failures.symptom: The fast test tier on the merged branch spent 28 minutes in semgrep: tests calling run_scan(use_adapters=False) ran every external analyzer after an earlier test in the same process had registered them; three such tests had been marked slow (ARB-046) to work around it.
failures.how_detected: a fast-tier run on the integration branch that took 28 minutes instead of two; agent report during ARB-046 named the mechanism
failures.root_cause: run_scan's use_adapters flag only guarded register_adapters(); the probe registry is module-global, so once registered the analyzers were ordinary probes and the scan loop ran them for every later scan whatever the flag said.
failures.fix_summary: The scan loop skips a probe marked external (ARB-047) when use_adapters is False and no explicit only= names it, with the outcome reason 'external analyzers disabled for this run'; an explicit only= still wins.
failures.prevention_notes: A flag that promises to keep something out of a run is enforced where the run happens, not only where the thing is registered; the regression test registers an external probe first and asserts the flag still skips it. Fast tier: 28 minutes to 1 minute 53 seconds.

failures.title: The HTML report built its 'Read first' block and never rendered it
failures.symptom: render_html assembled bluf_html (partial-scan fraction, withheld grade, skipped probes, scope notes) and the HTML page never contained it: the Markdown report showed the caveats, the HTML showed a clean-looking table with nothing above it. ruff F841 reported the local as never used.
failures.how_detected: ruff F841 on the ARB-049 self-scan
failures.root_cause: The commit that added the block (c86ba7b) interpolated it into the Markdown template and built the HTML string but left {bluf_html} out of the HTML f-string; no test rendered an HTML report with a caveat to show.
failures.fix_summary: The HTML template interpolates {bluf_html} between the grade banner and the severity cards.
failures.prevention_notes: An unused local that holds rendered output is a rendering that never happened; the regression test renders a report with a skipped probe and asserts the block sits above the findings table in both formats.

failures.title: pr-check.yml and train.yml pin their actions to mutable major tags
failures.symptom: Every `uses:` in .github/workflows (actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-python@v5, actions/cache@v4, actions/upload-artifact@v4, github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3) names a tag the action owner can repoint. At .github/workflows/pr-check.yml:66.
failures.how_detected: arbiter arbiter/supply.unpinned-action finding f:f351df511ecf and semgrep github-actions-mutable-action-tag finding f:6450363da7ac, adjudicated true positive in the ARB-049 sweep
failures.root_cause: The workflows were written with the major-tag convention GitHub's own examples use; nothing in the repository checks that a third-party ref is immutable.
failures.fix_summary: pr-check.yml and train.yml name each action's commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment (checkout 11d5960a v4, setup-python a26af69b v5, cache 0057852b v4, upload-artifact ea165f8d v4, upload-sarif 9f759ee6 v3), resolved with git ls-remote --tags.
failures.no_test_reason: A workflow file has no unit test; the self-gate's supply.unpinned-action rule is the check that catches a return to tags.
failures.prevention_notes: Fix is to pin each action to a commit SHA with the version in a trailing comment and let Dependabot move it; outside the ARB-049 scope (src, tests, arbiter.yaml, baseline, ledger), left open.

failures.title: test_a_bad_plan_path_fails_loudly accepted any exception as the loud failure
failures.symptom: The test wrapped run_scan in pytest.raises(Exception), so a TypeError from a mistyped argument would have passed it as readily as the engine's refusal of a non-plan document. At tests/test_probes_iac.py:201.
failures.how_detected: arbiter ruff/B017 finding f:1186bedac20c, adjudicated true positive in the ARB-049 sweep
failures.root_cause: The test was written before the engine settled on RuntimeError for a bad plan path and was never tightened.
failures.fix_summary: pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match='not a Terraform plan').
failures.prevention_notes: A loud failure is a named exception; a test that accepts Exception proves only that something broke.

failures.title: The suppression census counted # noqa inside Python strings and docstrings
failures.symptom: assurance.blanket-suppression reported 18 sites on the self-scan of which 16 were prose or fixtures: this module's own docstring explaining what a bare # noqa means, core.py's decision comment, and the strings the probe's tests write into temporary files.
failures.how_detected: arbiter arbiter/assurance.blanket-suppression finding f:bdf050c868b3 and its siblings, adjudicated false positive in the ARB-049 sweep
failures.root_cause: _suppressions ran the regex census over the whole file text; for Python a hash inside a string literal is not a comment, and the docs-role exclusion added for README did not cover source and test files.
failures.fix_summary: _python_comments_only blanks everything the tokenizer does not report as a COMMENT token, positions kept, before the census runs over a Python file; a file that will not tokenize keeps the regex view.
failures.prevention_notes: A directive is a comment; the third probe to blank prose before matching (after the import scanner's docstrings and the disabled-check scanner's comments) and the same lesson.

failures.title: A requirement quoted inside a one-line manifest list was read as undeclared
failures.symptom: authored.undeclared-import reported tree_sitter as declared in no manifest although pyproject.toml declares it in the ast extra; the extra is written as a one-line list.
failures.how_detected: arbiter arbiter/authored.undeclared-import finding f:6d0f30bbc168, adjudicated false positive in the ARB-049 sweep
failures.root_cause: _declared_dependencies anchored both name patterns to the start of a line, so only the first name of an inline list (or none, when the line starts with the extra's key) was read.
failures.fix_summary: A third pattern reads every quoted requirement followed by a version operator, an extras bracket, a marker or a closing quote, wherever it sits on the line.
failures.prevention_notes: Manifest formats put several requirements on one line; a reader anchored to line starts is a reader of the first column only.

failures.title: An environment-variable name assigned to a credential-named symbol was reported as a hardcoded credential
failures.symptom: Code scanning on upstream OmniEngineering PR #3: 'Hardcoded credential assigned to SEMANTIC_API_KEY_ENV' (arbiter/secrets.assigned-credential) for SEMANTIC_API_KEY_ENV = "OMNI_GRAPH_SEMANTIC_API_KEY" in omni_graph.py.
failures.how_detected: code scanning alert on upstream OmniEngineering PR #3, from the SARIF omni gate uploaded
failures.root_cause: _credential_finding judged the value by entropy and character classes; an upper-case identifier with underscores has two classes and enough entropy to pass, and nothing looked at the shape of the value or at a symbol suffix (_ENV, _VAR, _NAME) that says the symbol holds a name rather than a secret.
failures.fix_summary: _credential_finding returns None for a value shaped like an environment-variable name (^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{2,}$) and for a symbol whose suffix is _env, _env_var, _envvar, _var, _name or _key_name; a real credential beside it still fires.
failures.prevention_notes: The regression test holds three name-holding assignments that must be silent and a live-looking key beside them that must fire.

failures.title: An analyzer with no ruleset was reported as a clean run
failures.symptom: With ~/.cache/arbiter/semgrep-rules absent, semgrep exited 7 ('unable to find a config') and the report showed semgrep: ran, 0 findings; with a primed cache it replayed the previous run's 11 findings.
failures.how_detected: Planted-bug scan of the interview starters, 2026-10-20
failures.root_cause: Adapter.run only treated a non-ok exit as an error when stdout was empty; semgrep prints a JSON error body, so the failed run parsed as zero results. The ruleset was never declared as a requirement, so nothing checked for it before the cache lookup, and the cache key does not cover the rules directory.
failures.fix_summary: Adapters declare required files ([requires] files, {cache} resolved at check time); Probe.prevented reports a missing one as not assessed before any cache replay; an exit outside ok_exit with no parsed rows is an error carrying the tool's first error message. semgrep declares its pinned ruleset marker.
failures.prevention_notes: A tool's exit code and an empty result are separate facts; check the exit code whenever nothing parsed. Any input an analyzer needs besides its binary is declared in its manifest.

failures.title: import arbiter.lang_rules before arbiter.probes raised a circular ImportError
failures.symptom: ImportError: cannot import name 'register_lang_rules' from partially initialized module 'arbiter.lang_rules' (most likely due to a circular import)
failures.how_detected: reproduced while writing docs/gaps-and-next-steps.md (2026-10-21)
failures.root_cause: lang_rules imported PACKS and ProbeContext from probes at module level, while probes imports lang_rules at its end to register the packs; importing lang_rules first started probes, which then asked for a name lang_rules had not defined yet. The suite never saw it because conftest and earlier tests imported probes first, and two test files papered over it with an import-order line.
failures.fix_summary: lang_rules defines AST_PACKS from its own path and imports ProbeContext under TYPE_CHECKING only; the import-order workaround lines in tests were removed
failures.prevention_notes: every module is imported first in its own fresh subprocess in the test suite, so a new top-level back-import fails CI whatever the import order of other tests

failures.title: controls._probe_of mapped arbiter/<lang>.* to <lang>, so language-pack controls always read not assessed
failures.symptom: _probe_of('arbiter/python.x') returned 'python'; a control satisfied by a language-pack rule resolved to not_assessed with reason 'probe did not run' even when lang_python ran clean
failures.how_detected: code reading for docs/gaps-and-next-steps.md and ARB-062 criterion 5 (2026-10-21)
failures.root_cause: _probe_of mapped native rule-id heads through a fixed table and fell back to the head itself; language packs register their probe as lang_<pack>, which the table never knew, and no test evaluated a control backed by a pack rule
failures.fix_summary: _probe_of returns lang_<pack> for any head that names a shipped language pack, read from lang_rules.load_packs() so a new pack needs no edit
failures.prevention_notes: every shipped pack rule id is checked to map to a registered probe name, and a real scan per language asserts the control reads satisfied

failures.title: Repeated defects with identical evidence in one file collapsed into one finding
failures.symptom: six identical catch {} (or rescue Exception) in one file reported once: one fingerprint, and engine._dedupe kept one per id
failures.how_detected: code reading for docs/gaps-and-next-steps.md (2026-10-21)
failures.root_cause: the fingerprint deliberately excludes line numbers so a baseline survives reformatting; with nothing else to tell same-evidence sites in one file apart, they shared an id and deduplication by id treated them as one defect
failures.fix_summary: core.assign_occurrences numbers the distinct sites of one id before _dedupe (occurrence 0 keeps the old id); legacy baselines, suppressions by id and diffs from legacy reports match every repeat; arbiter baseline --migrate rewrites a legacy baseline
failures.prevention_notes: a real scan of six repeats must yield six ids, and the gate on a legacy baseline must stay green on unchanged code

failures.title: controls._probe_of mapped house/<id> to 'house', so a control backed by a house rule always read not assessed
failures.symptom: _probe_of('house/x') returned 'house'; no probe has that name (house rules come from house_rules, ast_query ones from house_rules_ast), so a control mapped to a house rule resolved to not_assessed with 'probe did not run' even after both house probes ran clean
failures.how_detected: ARB-062 round 2 controls review (2026-10-22), reading _probe_of for every emitted prefix
failures.root_cause: The house/ prefix is not arbiter/-prefixed, so it skipped the native-probe table (whose 'house' entry only matched the never-emitted arbiter/house.*) and fell through to the bare head. Two probes emit house/ ids and which one depends on the rule's type in arbiter.yaml, which _probe_of never saw; FAIL-053's test enumerated language packs only, not every emitted prefix
failures.fix_summary: house/<id> maps to house_rules_ast for an ast_query rule and house_rules otherwise, using the rule types from the scan configuration (engine passes house_rule_types(config)); a report read without its configuration (arbiter controls on report.json) requires both house probes, so an ast_query rule is never read as assessed when tree-sitter was missing; a house id absent from the configuration reads not assessed. The dead arbiter/house entry is removed
failures.prevention_notes: Every rule-id prefix the scanner can emit is enumerated from the source (literal arbiter/<head>. ids, house/, each language pack, each adapter manifest) and asserted to map to a registered probe; a real scan over every planted bad tree plus both house rule types asserts each finding's recorded probe equals _probe_of(rule_id)

failures.title: Model label reasons quoted credential-shaped DB URLs from corpus code
failures.symptom: omni gate (arbiter gate) failed with 2 new secrets.pg-url findings in tools/gold/labels/history/gold-model-v1.jsonl after the file was moved; labeller reasons quoted postgres://user:pass@host URLs seen in the excerpt
failures.how_detected: omni gate
failures.root_cause: label_models.parse_answer stored the model's reason verbatim; _mask_secrets masks the excerpt but does not cover inline DB-URL credentials, and a reason can quote code back
failures.fix_summary: parse_answer passes reasons through mask_reason (_mask_secrets plus DB-URL credentials); existing label files' reasons re-masked
failures.prevention_notes: Anything a model returns that may quote corpus code is masked before it is written to a tracked file

failures.title: Installer pin test assumed shell literals
failures.symptom: The fast suite failed because test_install_script_pins_every_version could not find version literals in tools/install_tools.sh after the pins moved to tooling.json.
failures.how_detected: python -m pytest -q -rs -m 'not slow'
failures.root_cause: The regression test encoded the old implementation detail (literal constants in the shell script) instead of asserting the behavior that versions come from one shared catalog.
failures.fix_summary: Updated the installer test to load the catalog and assert the installer uses its version, Semgrep rules, and grammar fields.
failures.prevention_notes: Tests for tool pinning now assert the shared catalog is authoritative rather than depending on where its literals are stored.

failures.title: Installer accepted analyzer version drift
failures.symptom: Tool lock verification found Ruff 0.17.1 where the committed lock requires 0.15.11; tools/install_tools.sh reported any existing binary as installed without checking its version.
failures.how_detected: arbiter tools verify .arbiter/tooling.lock.json
failures.root_cause: The install helper equated command presence with the pinned capability, so it bypassed installation for a mismatched executable and made the pinned installer nondeterministic.
failures.fix_summary: The installer now checks exact analyzer versions before accepting existing binaries and reports when the pinned binary is still unavailable on PATH; CI verification enforces the committed lock.
failures.prevention_notes: The installer pin test uses a fake old Ruff binary and requires the mismatch to remain visible; the CI lock check then fails on any remaining version drift.

failures.title: Cache install test mocked staging path
failures.symptom: Focused tooling tests failed with KeyError after the installer published the staged cache under its final lock-keyed path.
failures.how_detected: Focused pytest run
failures.root_cause: The fake version probe keyed expected output by the staging executable's absolute path, but installation atomically renamed the staging directory before the final verification pass, so the mock no longer recognized the executable.
failures.fix_summary: Keyed fake version output by analyzer binary name, which remains stable across the staging-to-cache rename.
failures.prevention_notes: Tests of staged publication should identify executables by stable tool identity rather than temporary filesystem paths.

failures.title: Adapter cache guidance changed without a lock
failures.symptom: The fast suite reported that a missing adapter rules file no longer advised running tools/install_tools.sh when the repository had no tooling lock.
failures.how_detected: Full fast pytest suite
failures.root_cause: The lock-aware dependency callback always displayed the new tools-install command, even when it had selected the pre-existing machine-wide cache path and installer.
failures.fix_summary: Choose the install guidance from the selected cache source: arbiter tools install for a lock-managed cache, tools/install_tools.sh for the existing global cache.
failures.prevention_notes: Adapter dependency guidance must match whether its files resolve through a lock-managed cache or the existing global cache.

failures.title: Trivy-only locks used the global data cache
failures.symptom: A Trivy lock without semgrep_rules resolved the data cache to the global Arbiter cache, so missing database preflight checked a global path instead of the lock-keyed cache.
failures.how_detected: Focused Trivy tooling and adapter tests
failures.root_cause: locked_cache_dir returned a lock-keyed path only when semgrep_rules was present; it did not recognize Trivy as another lock-scoped data consumer.
failures.fix_summary: Resolve the lock-keyed cache when the lock includes Trivy and add a missing-database preflight regression test.
failures.prevention_notes: When a new adapter owns lock-scoped data, add its lock entry to cache resolution and test the isolated preflight path.

failures.title: Tooling tests assumed analyzer list order
failures.symptom: Focused tests failed after Trivy was added because tests selected Ruff with analyzers[-2] and the plan test omitted the new analyzer.
failures.how_detected: Focused Trivy tooling and adapter tests
failures.root_cause: Tests coupled tool identity to catalog position instead of the stable analyzer name, so adding a catalog entry changed which tool they exercised.
failures.fix_summary: Select Ruff by name and include Trivy in the expected applicable tool set.
failures.prevention_notes: Tooling tests must identify catalog items by stable names rather than array positions.

failures.title: docs/precision.md carried a stale second copy of itself after the round-4 merge
failures.symptom: docs/precision.md was 825 lines: after 'Current numbers' a line read '## Model verification`), which supplies' followed by a 280-line older copy of Definition, Tiers, Ledger, Label format and Current numbers (the pre-ARB-065 wording, without the population-weighted claim), and only then the real Model verification section
failures.how_detected: review while updating the Tiers section for ARB-100 (grep '^## ' showed every heading twice)
failures.root_cause: The round-4 branch merge (r4-weights into round4-integration, c70c113) resolved a conflict in the document's intro paragraph by keeping both sides' bodies: one side's tail was spliced into the other's heading, and nothing checks a document for duplicated headings
failures.fix_summary: Lines 405-684 (the garbled heading through the line before the real '## Model verification') removed; the newer first half is the one kept
failures.no_test_reason: a documentation merge artefact; tests/test_docs.py checks links and anchors, not duplicate headings, and a one-off doc check is not worth a permanent test
failures.prevention_notes: After a merge that touched a long document, grep its H2 headings once; a repeated heading is a merge that kept both sides

failures.title: default view hid ~all findings (only one verified rule); no check measured what a user sees by default
failures.symptom: After ARB-100 the default report showed verified findings only. With one verified rule (supply.unpinned-action), a default scan listed 0 of 404 active findings on fixtures/planted and 0 of 127 on fixtures/ai-corpus, and on the AI-written-code corpus showed roughly none of the known mistakes; legacy-platform showed its 2 unpinned-Action lows and hid 71 findings including 3 criticals. Every test, snapshot, precision and perf guard stayed green.
failures.how_detected: owner review of PR #17 (round5-integration)
failures.root_cause: In the recommendation and the brief, not the implementation. ARB-100 was specified as 'what is shown by default is what is 99% right', which conflated two decisions: what may block a build (where a 99% bar is right) and what a reader is shown (where hiding unconfirmed findings defeats a tool whose purpose is to catch mistakes, especially in AI-written code). Nobody weighed the brief against how few rules were verified (one), so the default view was built correctly to a wrong requirement. And no check measured the default view: the regression guard, the precision guard and the snapshots all read raw findings, which ARB-100 deliberately left untouched, so a change that hid everything from users moved no number.
failures.fix_summary: ARB-103: report.show defaults to all (verified first, advisory then inferred, each labelled with whether it can block the gate); gate.tier_mode stays tiered so only verified findings block; --verified-only / report.show: verified is the opt-in; MCP show defaults to all; SARIF caps non-gating results at warning instead of note.
failures.prevention_notes: tools/regression_guard.py check now scans targets marked default_view (planted, ai-corpus) under the default configuration and fails if the default view lists fewer findings than the scan has active ones; test_default_view_hides_no_finding runs it in the fast suite. A requirement that changes a default should state what a user sees under it on the in-tree corpora before it is accepted.

failures.title: Copilot CLI: an empty --available-tools leaves every tool on; a blind-packet seat read a file
failures.symptom: Building the panel's Copilot seat, a canary test run with 'copilot -p ... --available-tools' (no value) in an empty temp dir called the 'view' tool and printed the canary file's contents. A labelling seat that can read files can be steered by a packet's text to read or leak anything under its path allowance.
failures.how_detected: canary test during ARB-122 provider hardening (before any panel label was made)
failures.root_cause: The flag was read as 'restrict tools to this list' with an empty list meaning none. Copilot 1.0.103 treats an empty --available-tools as not given, so the default tool set stays. Nothing checked the hardening empirically: tool-off flags were assumed from --help wording, not tested against a canary.
failures.fix_summary: CopilotProvider passes --available-tools=panel_no_tool (a tool name that does not exist, so no tool is exposed; re-tested: the canary was not read), denies shell/write/url and every URL, disables built-in MCP servers, custom instructions and the temp-dir allowance, and refuses any answer whose events carry a tool request or tool execution. Every seat's provider refuses tool-using answers the same way.
failures.prevention_notes: A provider's tool-off configuration is proven with a canary file in its temp dir before the seat is trusted (docs/precision.md, Panel). The command each provider builds is asserted in tests, and a tool event in any answer refuses it at run time, so a CLI release that changes flag meaning fails closed.

failures.title: supply.unpinned-action reported quoted SHA pins and docker:// digests as unpinned, and never checked docker:// tags
failures.symptom: A pinned step written `uses: "actions/checkout@<40-hex>"` or with single quotes was reported as pinned to the mutable ref `<sha>"`; `uses: docker://alpine@sha256:<64-hex>` (a digest pin) was reported as action `docker://alpine` at ref `sha256:...`; `uses: docker://alpine:3.18` (a mutable tag) matched nothing and was never reported. This on the one rule declared verified (ledger 690/0).
failures.how_detected: owner/agent review of the pinning methods the rule claims to cover (ARB-130 brief), confirmed by reading the regex
failures.root_cause: The rule regex-matched YAML: `uses:[ \t]*([^\s@]+)@([^\s#]+)`. The character classes excluded whitespace, @ and # but not quotes, so a quoted scalar carried its quotes into both groups and the 40-hex test failed. docker:// references are container images, but splitting at @ treated a digest as an action ref, and with no @ a tag was skipped. The 690 labels behind the verified claim never sampled a quoted or docker:// reference (the development corpora hold 6 quoted and 2 docker:// uses in all), so 0 FP said nothing about those shapes.
failures.fix_summary: uses: values read through PyYAML's node API (quotes stripped by the parser, line numbers from marks); the fallback line pattern for non-YAML CI files excludes quotes and requires the closing one; docker:// references routed to supply.unpinned-container-image (digest = pinned); composite action.yml checked.
failures.prevention_notes: Structured files are parsed, not regex-matched (supply.py module docstring). Two mutations in tools/mutate_tests.py (quoted-uses-ref, docker-uses-read-as-action) put each defect back and require its test to fail. docs/precision.md records that the verified rule's population changed and that the new shapes are unlabelled until the next labelling round.

failures.title: A scanned repository's own arbiter.yaml could label its findings verified and switch off its gate
failures.symptom: A target shipping precision: {ledger: ledger.json, verified_rules: ['*']} with a ledger whose bar was 0.0 had every finding tiered 'verified ... measured at least 99% precise'; a target setting gate.fail_on.severity: null (or 'Critical') had a gate that could never fail. Both from the default scan of the target with no --config.
failures.how_detected: core audit of main 8a12926 (SUMMARY-docs-platform.md item 1)
failures.root_cause: load_config treated the file found in the target root exactly like one the operator passed with --config, and merged every key including precision and gate over DEFAULTS. load_ledger merged the ledger's own bar over DEFAULT_BAR, so a ledger could lower the bar it is judged by. Ledger paths were read as given, so a config could point at any file.
failures.fix_summary: restrict_target_config drops precision/verify and any gate key that would loosen the gate from a target-root config, recording each drop in scan_scope.config.ignored, which console/markdown/PR render; effective_bar floors the ledger bar at DEFAULT_BAR; resolve_ledger_path resolves relative to the config file and refuses escapes.
failures.prevention_notes: Any new config key that decides what is called verified or what can fail the gate must be added to TARGET_FORBIDDEN_KEYS or the tighten-only gate rules in restrict_target_config; test_target_config_trust covers the current keys.

failures.title: A repository in languages without a rule pack scored 99/100 with nothing marked not assessed
failures.symptom: semgrep's own Kotlin/Scala/Swift test files (134 ruleid: lines) scored overall 99.4 at 94% coverage, gate PASS, security claim scope 'complete'; no probe, note or abstention named the 2,000 unread source lines.
failures.how_detected: core audit of main 8a12926 (item 2)
failures.root_cause: Coverage is the share of applicable probe checks that ran. A lang_* probe for a language absent from the tree is inapplicable and leaves the denominator, and no outcome stood in for the languages present that have no pack, so a tree nobody could assess looked like a tree with nothing to assess. Swift and Scala were not even recognised as languages.
failures.fix_summary: Inventory recognises the common unsupported languages; lang_rules.not_assessed_outcome adds one skipped applicable lang_unsupported outcome sized like the missing packs; scan_scope.languages_not_assessed lists them; the grade is withheld above 50% unassessed source lines.
failures.prevention_notes: When adding a language to LANG_BY_EXT without a pack, NON_PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGES decides whether it is source; test_every_recognised_programming_language_without_a_pack_is_unassessed covers the common ones.

failures.title: --only-files with a dotfile or unknown path read zero files and the gate passed
failures.symptom: --only-files .husky/pre-commit read 0 files (files_changed 0) and the gate passed; --only-files nope.py did the same; docs/ci.md said an empty selection refuses.
failures.how_detected: core audit of main 8a12926 (item 4)
failures.root_cause: engine.run_scan normalised each path with str.lstrip('./'), which strips a set of characters, not a prefix, turning .husky into husky; and nothing checked that a requested path existed in the inventory or that files_changed was non-zero.
failures.fix_summary: _requested_path strips only a literal leading ./ and relativises absolute paths under a target; a requested path not in the inventory, or a selection that reads zero files, raises RuntimeError naming it.
failures.prevention_notes: Never use lstrip to remove a path prefix; the comment in adapters.to_findings and this entry both say why.

failures.title: An analyzer failing inside its ok_exit codes was recorded as ran with 0 findings
failures.symptom: gitleaks with a malformed .gitleaks.toml (FTL, exit 1, no report file) went from 1 finding to 0 and stayed status ran; semgrep exit 0 with empty or non-JSON stdout, a renamed results key, ruff exit 1 with no stdout, and bandit errors[] for an unparsable file were all 'ran', 0 findings, counted toward coverage.
failures.how_detected: core audit of main 8a12926 (item 5), fake binaries
failures.root_cause: Adapter.parse_output returned [] for empty, non-JSON and wrong-shaped output alike, and Adapter.run only raised when the exit code was outside ok_exit AND there were no rows; gitleaks and ruff reuse exit 1 for failure, so the code could not tell failure from findings, and nothing read a tool's own errors list.
failures.fix_summary: Adapter.decode/rows_of raise AdapterOutputError for output not matching the manifest; map.errors declares a tool's own error list and any non-warning entry raises AnalyzerErrors (findings set aside per CI-7, counted in the reason); stderr's last line is quoted in the reason.
failures.prevention_notes: A new adapter manifest should declare map.errors where the tool reports its own failures; an adapter's empty answer must be a readable empty document, never missing output.

failures.title: House-rule globs via fnmatch missed root files and src/a.py, so forbid policies were false-clean
failures.symptom: content_match with the default files '**/*' never matched root.py; files: 'src/**/*.py' never matched src/a.py; on Windows fnmatch folded case so a rule matched different files than in Linux CI.
failures.how_detected: core audit of main 8a12926 (item 6)
failures.root_cause: fnmatch is not a path matcher: '*' crosses '/', and '**/' requires a literal slash, so '**/*' needs at least one directory and 'src/**/*.py' needs at least one directory under src.
failures.fix_summary: src/arbiter/globs.py: a globstar matcher (* within a segment, ** across segments, [...] classes, case-sensitive); probe_house_rules and probe_house_rules_ast use it for files: and paths:.
failures.prevention_notes: Path globs in house rules go through arbiter.globs.match; fnmatch stays only where its semantics are documented (gitignore reader, suppression path globs, pack files:).

failures.title: A target-root suppress entry or severity override hid findings so the repository passed its own gate
failures.symptom: suppress: [{reason: temporary}] in the scanned repository's own arbiter.yaml set both findings aside: overall 100.0, gate PASS, no suppressed count in the scorecard. severity_overrides {'*': info} took every finding below every threshold.
failures.how_detected: core audit of main 8a12926 (CORE-022)
failures.root_cause: ARB-143 restricted precision, verify and the gate keys of a target-root config but left suppress, probes.severity_overrides and score alone as features the target is meant to use; each is a second way to pass one's own gate.
failures.fix_summary: restrict_target_config drops suppress and probes.severity_overrides and a score.coverage_threshold below the default from a target-root config, noting each in scan_scope.config.ignored; --config is trusted in full and the self-gate commands pass --config arbiter.yaml.
failures.prevention_notes: Any key of a target-root config that can remove, downgrade or re-weigh a finding goes through restrict_target_config; the trust rule is in docs/configuration.md.

failures.title: An empty, docs-only or binary-only directory scored 100 with the gate passed
failures.symptom: scan of an empty directory, a README-only directory and a directory holding one .bin: overall 100.0, coverage 0.945, withheld False, gate PASS.
failures.how_detected: core audit of main 8a12926 (CORE-017)
failures.root_cause: compute_scorecard measures probe-check coverage; every applicable probe ran over nothing and found nothing, and nothing asked whether any file a probe reads had been read.
failures.fix_summary: Inventory.assessable_files names text files in roles source/test/config/iac/ci; when none was read the engine withholds the grade with withheld_by nothing_read and the gate fails on it.
failures.prevention_notes: A grade requires at least one assessable file read; withheld_by carries the cause to the gate.

failures.title: Files skipped for a NUL byte, size, BOM-less UTF-16, a symlinked directory or a vendored path vanished from the report
failures.symptom: a.py with a NUL in a comment, a 2.4MB .py, a UTF-16 file without BOM, a symlinked src/ and app/vendor/h.py: 0 findings, 100/100, gate PASS; grep of report.json for their names found nothing. A file symlink to /outside was read and its content echoed into the evidence.
failures.root_cause: walk_repo marked such files binary/data or pruned the directory and recorded nothing; coverage counted probe checks, not files, so a file nobody read cost nothing.
