failures.fix_summary: walk_repo appends every skipped file and directory with a reason to Inventory.skipped; scan_scope.skipped reports them; a files_not_read outcome sits in the coverage denominator; above 50% of source-like files skipped the grade is withheld; a file symlink leaving the tree is not read; BOM-less UTF-16 is detected by NUL stride and named.
failures.prevention_notes: Nothing leaves the walk silently: a skip is an entry with a reason, and source-like skips count against coverage.

failures.title: --changed counted a changed file as read when no probe read it, and a delete-only change said nothing
failures.symptom: a PR moving code into dist/: files_read 1, 0 findings, gate PASS; a changed file with a NUL byte: files_changed 1, lines_read 0, gate PASS; a PR that only deleted files: files_read 0, gate PASS with no note.
failures.how_detected: core audit of main 8a12926 (CORE-020)
failures.root_cause: narrow() counted a selected path as read if it was in the inventory, binary or generated included; git_changed filters deletions out, so a delete-only change looked like no change.
failures.fix_summary: narrow() counts only text, non-generated files as read and lists changed_not_read with reasons; git_deleted names deletions; evaluate_gate fails when changed files exist and none was read; the renderings say what happened.
failures.prevention_notes: files_read means a probe read the file; a changed path that was not read is listed, never counted.

failures.title: Gate severity typos, selector-less permanent suppressions and withheld grades all passed the gate
failures.symptom: gate.fail_on.severity: Critical or crtical (and new: hgih): gate PASS beside a critical, reasons empty. suppress entry with only a reason: both findings suppressed forever. probes disabled in the target config: coverage 3%, grade withheld, gate PASS.
failures.how_detected: core audit of main 8a12926 (CORE-022/023/025)
failures.root_cause: sev_at_least returned False for an unknown threshold and nothing validated the name; the apply_suppressions docstring said expiry was mandatory but nothing checked it or required a selector; coverage_below defaulted to None so a withheld grade had no bearing on the gate.
failures.fix_summary: check_gate_config normalises severities and raises on unknown names; suppression_problems enforces reason, expires and a selector at load and in apply_suppressions; Scorecard.withheld_by names the cause and evaluate_gate fails on a withheld grade unless the operator narrowed the scan (partial, probes_selected).
failures.prevention_notes: Every gate and suppression key is validated at load; a withheld grade fails the gate by default and only --config can switch that off.

failures.title: install_tools.sh called python3 by name; Windows Store alias broke it
failures.symptom: tools/install_tools.sh exited 2 with 'Python was not found; run without arguments to install from the Microsoft Store' and 'Could not read tool versions from src/arbiter/tooling.json'; test_install_script_never_fails_a_build and test_install_script_does_not_accept_an_unpinned_existing_binary failed, so omni gate refused every commit on that machine
failures.how_detected: omni gate on a Windows laptop while consolidating local branches
failures.root_cause: 3561ecc (2026-10-23) added a catalog read that runs bare python3. On Windows python3 is often the Store alias in WindowsApps: it is on PATH, so command -v finds it, but it only prints an install hint and exits non-zero. Other call sites used command -v python3 || command -v python, which has the same blind spot. Windows CI runners have a working python3, so CI never saw it
failures.fix_summary: Pick the interpreter once by asking python3 then python to run 'import sys' and taking the first that succeeds; every Python step in the script uses that choice
failures.prevention_notes: Probe interpreters by running them, not by command -v; the Store alias defeats PATH checks

failures.title: Path traversal assertion message mismatch
failures.symptom: The focused evaluator test failed because the path-traversal guard raised 'must stay within its repository' while the test expected 'relative path'.
failures.how_detected: python -m pytest -q tests/test_realvuln_conformance.py
failures.root_cause: The new test asserted a wording fragment that did not match the evaluator's intentional, more specific rejection message; the implementation behavior was correct.
failures.fix_summary: Updated the assertion to match the explicit repository-boundary error contract; the focused suite now passes.
failures.prevention_notes: Check expected failure messages against the validated input-boundary contract, not an assumed generic phrase.

failures.title: Label-count test bypassed manifest consistency check
failures.symptom: The focused evaluator test received 'manifest aggregate_metadata mismatch' before reaching the intended ground-truth label-count mismatch assertion.
failures.how_detected: python -m pytest -q tests/test_realvuln_conformance.py
failures.root_cause: The test changed one repository's expected positive count but did not update the manifest aggregate, so the evaluator correctly rejected the internally inconsistent manifest first.
failures.fix_summary: Updated the test to keep candidate aggregate metadata internally consistent while deliberately mismatching the loaded ground-truth count.
failures.prevention_notes: When testing layered validation, keep earlier-layer inputs valid so the test reaches the intended rejection boundary.

failures.title: Benchmark manifest candidate schema mismatch
failures.symptom: Draft 2020-12 validation rejected the approved RealVuln manifest: candidate_sources was not a root property, dotted candidate IDs were disallowed, and the safe-trap aggregate key did not match the schema.
failures.how_detected: Draft202012Validator.check_schema and manifest validation during ARB-097
failures.root_cause: The existing schema placed candidate_sources at the benchmark-inventory item level instead of the manifest root; the new versioned candidate also exposed an overly narrow identifier pattern and a metadata key inconsistency.
failures.fix_summary: Moved candidate_sources to the manifest root, expanded its schema for pinned repository/license metadata, corrected candidate ID syntax and the aggregate key, and added a regression test for the approved subset.
failures.prevention_notes: Validate both JSON schema structure and manifest instances whenever adding a candidate source; exercise the checked-in candidate through the evaluator contract.

failures.title: Map benchmark ground-truth identifiers explicitly
failures.symptom: Retrieval stopped because the selected manifest key did not equal the internal repo_id in pinned ground-truth metadata.
failures.how_detected: Metadata-only lookup of the pinned GitHub ground-truth records.
failures.root_cause: The evaluator and retrieval path treated the manifest's benchmark directory slug as the ground-truth record identity, but RealVuln uses separate identifiers for those two namespaces.
failures.fix_summary: Added an explicit ground_truth_repo_id mapping to each selected source and validate the mapping independently from the local source key.
failures.prevention_notes: Keep external directory keys and embedded record IDs as separate validated fields; exercise a case where their values differ.

failures.title: Assert the evaluator's aggregate output contract
failures.symptom: Focused evaluator test failed with KeyError for an assumed confusion_matrix output key.
failures.how_detected: Focused pytest run for tests/test_realvuln_conformance.py.
failures.root_cause: The test assertion was rewritten without retrieving the evaluator's existing output contract, so its expected key names were guessed rather than grounded in the implementation.
failures.fix_summary: Changed the assertion to use the existing case_level_confusion, metrics and run fields, while retaining the distinct ground-truth ID regression case.
failures.prevention_notes: Inspect the current producer output contract before changing assertions and reconcile aggregate counts against every included fixture record.

failures.title: Use the benchmark directory key for metadata retrieval
failures.symptom: The GitHub content API request for a ground-truth record failed when the embedded record ID was used in the directory path.
failures.how_detected: Pinned metadata retrieval from the approved GitHub benchmark commit.
failures.root_cause: The archive folder is keyed by the manifest repo_id slug, while the JSON body carries a different ground_truth_repo_id; the path and embedded identity are separate namespaces.
failures.fix_summary: Retrieved metadata under the manifest repo_id path and separately validated the embedded ground_truth_repo_id.
failures.prevention_notes: Use the manifest directory key to locate records; use the explicit internal-ID mapping only to validate record identity.

failures.title: Normalize wrapped base64 API content before decoding
failures.symptom: Pinned GitHub contents metadata failed strict base64 decoding because the API content string contained line breaks.
failures.how_detected: Approved metadata retrieval from GitHub API.
failures.root_cause: The retrieval path enabled strict base64 validation without normalizing the whitespace GitHub wraps into content responses.
failures.fix_summary: Removed whitespace from the base64 content field before strict decoding; all 11 records then passed pin validation.
failures.no_test_reason: The retrieval procedure was a one-off aggregate-only acquisition command, not retained as product code; a network integration test would add unnecessary live API dependence. All 11 retrieved records were directly validated against the pinned IDs, versions, languages, and source commits.
failures.prevention_notes: Normalize documented API transport whitespace before strict decoding and validate the decoded record metadata.

failures.title: Validate ground-truth and published benchmark versions separately
failures.symptom: Acquisition validation rejected the pinned ground-truth record because its benchmark_version is 3.0.0 while the published RealVuln release is 3.1.0.
failures.how_detected: Pinned ground-truth metadata validation before scanning.
failures.root_cause: The evaluator compared the ground-truth record's benchmark_version against the published dataset release version, conflating distinct version fields.
failures.fix_summary: Validated the record benchmark_version and ground_truth_version against the manifest's ground_truth_version, while retaining 3.1.0 as the published benchmark version.
failures.prevention_notes: Keep publication-release and embedded ground-truth version contracts distinct and test the pinned metadata combination.

failures.title: Keep schema references within definition scope
failures.symptom: The manifest schema validation failed because evaluation_run referenced aggregateMetric and rateInterval definitions placed outside the JSON Schema $defs object.
failures.how_detected: Draft 2020-12 validation of docs/accuracy-benchmark-manifest.json against docs/accuracy-benchmark-manifest.schema.json.
failures.root_cause: The schema edit closed the $defs object before adding new reusable definitions, leaving valid JSON with unresolved JSON Schema references.
failures.fix_summary: Moved aggregateMetric and rateInterval into the existing $defs object; the manifest validates successfully.
failures.no_test_reason: The schema and manifest are validated directly with Draft202012Validator; adding jsonschema as a runtime test dependency is not justified for this documentation-only contract.
failures.prevention_notes: Validate schema references against the actual JSON Schema $defs structure after changing reusable definitions.

failures.title: Run completion tests in an environment with pytest installed
failures.symptom: The first omni gate attempt failed its impacted test suite because the default interpreter had no pytest module.
failures.how_detected: python omni gate before retrying with the isolated uv test environment.
failures.root_cause: The workspace interpreter had not been provisioned with the project development test dependencies, so the gate could not invoke pytest even though the code and tests were valid.
failures.fix_summary: Reran the gate through uv with the project test and runtime dependencies available; the impacted completion suite passed.
failures.no_test_reason: This was an environment provisioning issue rather than a product defect; the full fast test tier and the repeated Omni gate are the validation evidence.
failures.prevention_notes: Run Omni completion gates using an interpreter provisioned with the registered test-suite dependencies.

failures.title: Reject zero end lines when matching findings
failures.symptom: A finding location with end_line=0 was treated as if end_line were omitted and could match a labelled case.
failures.how_detected: Focused evaluator regression test added during code review.
failures.root_cause: The matcher used a truthiness fallback for end_line, conflating the malformed numeric value zero with a missing or null value.
failures.fix_summary: The matcher now falls back only when end_line is absent or null; zero remains invalid and cannot match.
failures.prevention_notes: Validate malformed numeric spans explicitly and cover boundary values in case-matching tests.

failures.title: Count all unassessed findings in the shared fixture
failures.symptom: The new zero-end-line regression test expected one unmatched finding but the evaluator correctly reported two.
failures.how_detected: Focused evaluator regression test run.
failures.root_cause: The test expectation counted the malformed finding but overlooked that the helper fixture already contained another unmatched CWE-89 finding.
failures.fix_summary: Updated the expected unassessed count to include both the invalid-span finding and the existing unmatched CWE-89 finding.
failures.prevention_notes: Compute expected aggregate counts from every finding in the shared fixture, including pre-existing unmatched cases.

failures.title: Adapter concurrency test compared against a fixed 2.0s and failed on slower machines
failures.symptom: tests/test_adapter_cache.py::test_two_adapters_run_at_once failed on a Windows laptop with 'two one-second adapters took 2.20s: they ran one after the other', on unmodified main (1ae32e8) as well as merged branches
failures.how_detected: omni gate while merging round 6 and ARB-110
failures.root_cause: The test required two one-second fake adapters to finish under 2.0s total. Scan overhead (process start-up, inventory, report) is not zero; on this machine it is ~1.2-1.8s, so a genuinely parallel run took 2.2s and was reported as serial. The bound ignored the cost the test itself adds
failures.fix_summary: Measure the scan with zero-second adapters first and require the parallel run to finish under that baseline plus 1.5s; serial costs baseline plus 2s. Added Fakes.reset_counts. Forcing parallel=1 still fails the test (3.70s against a 3.28s limit)
failures.prevention_notes: Timing assertions compare against a measured baseline from the same run, not a fixed wall-clock figure

failures.title: Hash-pinned accuracy report checked out with CRLF on Windows
failures.symptom: tests/test_realvuln_conformance.py::test_committed_multi_cwe_run_is_aggregate_only_and_digest_bound failed on Windows: sha256 703b11f7... against the manifest's 4776a16f...
failures.how_detected: omni gate while merging the ARB-110 branches
failures.root_cause: docs/accuracy-benchmark-manifest.json pins the sha256 of docs/accuracy-realvuln-multicwe-run.json as committed (LF). With no eol rule, a Windows checkout converts it to CRLF and the hash changes. CI runs that test on Linux, so it never failed there
failures.fix_summary: Added 'docs/accuracy-*.json text eol=lf' to .gitattributes, following the existing jsonl and tooling.json rules, and restored the report's committed bytes
failures.prevention_notes: Any file whose bytes are hashed elsewhere gets an eol=lf rule when it is added

failures.title: Windows CI reported the TypeScript pack as not assessed when tsx had not been downloaded
failures.symptom: test_controls_cwe_top25 [typescript] (not_assessed 12) and test_controls_lang_packs [typescript] (lang_typescript skipped) failed on windows-latest in PR #21 and in round 6's CI
failures.how_detected: PR #21 CI
failures.root_cause: The TypeScript pack needs both the typescript and tsx grammars. tree-sitter-language-pack downloads a grammar on first use and the Windows job skips install_tools.sh, so tsx was present or not depending on which test asked for it first. The tests' skip guard checked only the typescript grammar, so they ran and found the pack skipped for a missing tsx
failures.fix_summary: The CI install step downloads every default grammar from src/arbiter/tooling.json on all platforms
failures.prevention_notes: CI fetches grammars up front; nothing may depend on first-use downloads

failures.title: undeclared-import judged stdlib by the scanning interpreter, so 3.10 flagged import tomllib
failures.symptom: test_heldout_aggregate_snapshot_matches failed on ubuntu-latest 3.10 only: 163 -> 164 findings; reproduced in WSL, the extra finding was arbiter/authored.undeclared-import
failures.how_detected: PR #21 CI, reproduced on Python 3.10 in WSL
failures.root_cause: authored.py used sys.stdlib_module_names, which lists the modules of the Python running Arbiter, not of the code scanned. tomllib joined the stdlib in 3.11, so a 3.10 scan reported it as a missing dependency
failures.fix_summary: Union in the stdlib modules added after 3.10 (tomllib, annotationlib, compression and others); held-out total is 163 on both 3.10 and 3.11
failures.prevention_notes: Facts about scanned code must not come from the scanning interpreter's version

failures.title: Shipped GitHub Action used upload-sarif@v3, failing Arbiter's own self-gate
failures.symptom: The CI self-gate exited 1 with 'Action github/codeql-action/upload-sarif pinned to a mutable ref (v3)'
failures.how_detected: PR #21 CI self-gate
failures.root_cause: ci/github-action/action.yml, the action Arbiter ships to users, referenced upload-sarif by tag. FAIL-046 pinned every workflow action but this composite action was missed; supply.unpinned-action (verified tier) correctly blocks it
failures.fix_summary: Pinned to commit 9f759ee644a3e7c15c1390abf49868036c00067b, the same SHA pr-check.yml uses
failures.prevention_notes: Composite actions under ci/ are pinned like workflows

failures.title: label_models.py could not start the Claude CLI on Windows
failures.symptom: label run on Windows: FileNotFoundError [WinError 2] from subprocess.run(['claude', ...]); no label written
failures.how_detected: first r7 Python labelling run
failures.root_cause: npm installs claude as claude.cmd on Windows. subprocess without a shell does not run .cmd files, and running through a shell would mangle the multi-line prompts passed as arguments. Labelling had only ever run on Linux/macOS
failures.fix_summary: call_cli runs the bin/claude.exe that claude.cmd launches; elsewhere unchanged
failures.prevention_notes: Resolve CLI wrappers to their binary before passing multi-line arguments

failures.title: Labeller lost 11 answers: Claude's reply decoded as cp1252 on Windows
failures.symptom: 11 of 1,216 breadth labels failed with UnicodeDecodeError then TypeError: the JSON object must be str, not NoneType
failures.how_detected: label-breadth.log after the run
failures.root_cause: subprocess.run(text=True) uses the locale encoding (cp1252) on Windows; replies containing other characters could not be decoded, so stdout was None
failures.fix_summary: decode the CLI's output as UTF-8 with replacement; resumed run labelled the 11 remaining items
failures.prevention_notes: Every subprocess read in the labeller names its encoding
